# Product Knowledge: حصتي (Hissati) – LuggageShare peer-to-peer luggage space sharing platform

## What We Sell
Hissati (LuggageShare) is a Saudi peer-to-peer marketplace that connects travelers who have spare space in their luggage with people who need to send items between cities and countries. Travelers post upcoming trips with available weight and a price per kilogram, and senders browse trips, request bookings, coordinate via secure in-app chat, and pay through the platform, with payment released to the carrier after delivery is confirmed. It serves travelers looking to earn money from their trips and individuals seeking a cheaper, community-based alternative to traditional shipping.

## Core Value Proposition
Instead of paying for expensive shipping, send your items with someone already traveling your route — and if you're traveling, get paid for the empty space in your suitcase.

## Key Benefits
- Travelers earn money from unused luggage space on trips they are already taking
- Senders ship items between cities at lower cost than traditional courier/shipping services
- Payment held by the platform and released to the carrier only after the sender confirms delivery
- Trust built through verified Google accounts and two-way ratings and reviews
- Personal contact details protected via secure in-app chat that also keeps a record of agreements

## Features
- Trip posting with origin, destination, date, available weight, and price per kilogram
- Trip search and browsing by destination and date
- Booking requests with item details, weight, and photos
- Secure in-app messaging for coordinating pickup and handover
- Platform-mediated bank transfer payments with receipt upload and release upon delivery confirmation
- Mutual ratings and reviews after delivery
- Google account sign-in with automatic profile creation
- Reservation management and cancellation from the booking page
- In-app reporting of suspicious behavior and prohibited items
- Bilingual Arabic/English interface
- Support ticket system with categories (general, bug, billing, account, safety) and 24-hour response target
- Data access, update, deletion, and full data export from profile settings

## Use Cases
- An expat in Riyadh traveling to Cairo sells spare luggage kilos to people sending gifts or personal items to family in Egypt
- Someone in Jeddah sends a package to a contact in Dubai via a traveler on that route instead of using a courier
- A frequent business traveler between Dammam and Bahrain earns extra income on each regular trip
- A family sends personal belongings, documents, or non-perishable goods to relatives in Amman or Istanbul at lower cost

## Pricing
Free to join; travelers set their own price per kilogram for each trip. Hissati charges a service fee on every transaction (rate not published). Payment is made via bank transfer through the platform with a receipt upload as proof.

## Target Audience
Primarily consumers in Saudi Arabia and the Gulf/MENA region: (1) frequent travelers, expats, students, and business travelers flying routes such as Riyadh–Cairo, Jeddah–Dubai, Riyadh–Amman, Dammam–Bahrain, and Riyadh–Istanbul who want to monetize spare baggage allowance; (2) individuals and families who need to send personal items, gifts, documents, or small goods to relatives and contacts in other cities or countries more cheaply than courier services. Users must be 18+.

## Ideal Buyer Persona
This is a two-sided consumer marketplace based in Riyadh, so the 'buyer' is an individual adult (18+) rather than a corporate decision maker. The supply side is the frequent traveler: often a Saudi resident or an Arab expat (Egyptian, Jordanian and others) who regularly flies between Riyadh and cities such as Cairo, Jeddah, Dubai, Amman, Dammam, Bahrain or Istanbul. These are business travelers, professionals visiting family, and students. They often have unused baggage allowance and want to offset trip costs by setting their own price per kilogram. The demand side is the sender: someone who needs to get personal items, gifts, documents or small goods to family, friends or customers in another city or country. They find traditional courier and shipping services expensive, slow, or complicated for cross-border personal items. Both sides use Google sign-in, coordinate through in-app chat, and pay by bank transfer through the platform, with payment released after delivery is confirmed. Both care a lot about trust, so ratings, verified profiles and public meetup points matter. For the traveler, success means earning extra money with little effort on a trip they were already taking. For the sender, success means items arriving intact, cheaper and faster than with a courier, carried by a well-rated person they can trust.

## Integrations
- Google Sign-In (account authentication)
- Bank transfer payments (with receipt upload)

## What Makes Us Different
- Community-based peer-to-peer model using existing travelers rather than a dedicated logistics network, lowering cost
- Saudi-built and Arabic-first, focused on Gulf and MENA routes
- Escrow-style flow where the platform holds payment until delivery is confirmed rather than direct user-to-user payment
- Carrier-set per-kilogram pricing gives market-driven, flexible rates
- Trust layer of verified Google sign-in, ratings, and all communication kept in-app for an auditable record

## Social Proof & Case Studies
- No testimonials, case studies, customer logos, or usage statistics are published on the website
- Popular routes listed: Riyadh–Cairo, Jeddah–Dubai, Riyadh–Amman, Dammam–Bahrain, Riyadh–Istanbul

## Prospect Pain Points
- Traditional courier and international shipping services are expensive for small personal parcels sent between Saudi Arabia and nearby MENA countries
- Travelers waste unused baggage allowance and want to offset the cost of frequent trips
- Little trust when handing items to strangers informally, for example through WhatsApp or Facebook groups, with no verification, ratings or payment protection
- Payment risk and disputes in informal hand-carry arrangements, which the platform's escrow-style release after delivery addresses
- Sending gifts, documents or personal goods to family abroad (common for expat communities) is slow and complicated through formal channels

## Buying Triggers
When these events happen, prospects are most likely to buy:
- Booking an upcoming trip on a popular route (e.g., Riyadh to Cairo, Riyadh to Dubai, Riyadh to Istanbul) with spare luggage capacity
- Needing to urgently send gifts, documents or personal items to family or friends in another city or country, especially around holidays like Ramadan and Eid or the start of the school year
- Getting a high shipping quote from a courier for a small cross-border parcel
- A bad experience with informal hand-carry arrangements through social media groups

## Disqualifiers
Do NOT pursue prospects who:
- Businesses that need regular bulk, commercial, or freight shipping with guaranteed timelines, insurance and liability coverage (the platform says it is not a shipping company and is not liable for loss or damage)
- Senders of prohibited or high-risk items: cash, jewelry or goods worth more than 10,000 SAR, perishables without prior agreement, live animals, hazardous materials, weapons, counterfeit goods
- Users under 18 or without a Google account
- People outside the Saudi-centric GCC/MENA route network, with no travel or sending needs on the supported corridors

## Market Positioning
Hissati (حصتي) positions itself as a Saudi, Arabic-first, community-driven alternative to traditional courier and postal services. It connects travelers with spare luggage space to people who need to send items between cities, mainly on Gulf and MENA corridors such as Riyadh–Cairo, Jeddah–Dubai, Riyadh–Amman, Dammam–Bahrain and Riyadh–Istanbul. Its core pitch is twofold: senders get a more affordable and personal way to ship, and travelers can 'earn money from your trips' by monetizing empty luggage space at a self-set per-kg price. Hissati frames itself explicitly as an intermediary marketplace rather than a shipping company. It builds trust through verified Google sign-in, in-app secure chat, payments held by the platform until delivery is confirmed, two-way ratings, and a clear prohibited-items policy. The brand voice emphasizes trust, transparency and community, backed by a small Riyadh-based team. The website contains no explicit comparison pages or competitor mentions; the competitive framing is implicit ('instead of expensive shipping services').

## Tone & Voice
Friendly, practical, trust-focused, community-driven
